speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for providing your history. To begin our assessment, can you describe exactly how you have difficulty walking and whether you experience any specific sensory changes like numbness or tingling? Additionally, have you noticed any tremors, muscle weakness, or changes in your handwriting?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; the "drunk" gait and right-sided clumsiness suggest significant cerebellar involvement. Have you noticed any problems with your speech, such as slurring, or difficulties with eye movements like double vision? Also, do you have any known family history of similar neurological conditions or chronic alcohol use?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is a crucial piece of information, as natalizumab carries a known risk for progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML), which can present with cerebellar symptoms. Given your history of Crohn's and current medication, have you noticed any changes in your vision, such as new blind spots or color blindness, or any worsening of cognitive function like memory loss or confusion?

REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain_Axial.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI_Brain_Axial - Lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). T1/T2 images show multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy. The MRI findings of non-enhancing multifocal demyelinating lesions in the context of Crohn's disease treatment confirm this diagnosis. I recommend immediately discontinuing natalizumab and initiating antiviral therapy with famciclovir or cidofovir.
